overall_summary: Bitcoin is under pressure from fresh ETF outflows, rising Treasury yields, and strong jobs data that reduce near-term rate-cut hopes. Geopolitical flare-ups around Hormuz and new tariffs add to the risk-off backdrop, even as price holds 65K and a large call cluster sits overhead. The forward tone for crypto leans cautious until yields and flows stabilize.
key_points: Jobless claims plunge, cutting easing odds
Middle East tensions and tariffs escalate

items.title: Clarity Act Likely Misses Senate Summer Window
items.summary: Senate Majority Leader John Thune says the crypto market structure bill is unlikely to pass before the long summer recess, though floor debate might still start. Odds of 2026 passage have dropped sharply on prediction markets after ethics fights with Democrats. Traders should care because this was a key near-term catalyst for institutional comfort and upside bets; delay removes a major bullish overhang into August and raises the risk of further slippage into election season.
items.impact: Removes near-term regulatory catalyst, pressure on sentiment and call positions

items.title: Bitcoin Holds $65K as Oil Nears $100 and AI Stocks Crater
items.summary: Bitcoin settled near sixty-five thousand dollars even as Brent crude hit multi-month highs near ninety-eight dollars on the Iran conflict and Magnificent Seven tech stocks lost roughly eight hundred billion dollars on AI spending worries. Crypto largely ignored the equity rout and oil spike that previously rattled risk assets. This resilience matters because it hints at possible decoupling from the AI trade and shows buyers defending current levels amid macro noise ahead of the Fed meeting.
items.impact: Supports floor around 65k; positive signal of relative strength

items.title: Spot Bitcoin ETFs Snap Inflow Streak with $225M Outflows
items.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded two hundred twenty-five million dollars in net outflows on July twenty-third, ending a multi-day inflow run that had brought in nearly a billion dollars. Ether ETFs saw modest inflows in contrast. Traders should watch this closely because ETF flows have been a primary driver of spot demand; a one-day flip does not kill the structural bid but signals potential short-term cooling or profit-taking at these levels.
items.impact: Short-term demand headwind; tests whether buyers reload

items.title: $5 Billion Bullish Options Cluster Forms at $70-72K
items.summary: Deribit bitcoin options show nearly five billion dollars of open interest concentrated at the seventy and seventy-two thousand dollar call strikes, with calls heavily outnumbering puts. Much of the positioning was tied to Clarity Act optimism, though some unwinding has begun as passage odds fell. This is important for traders because large call walls can act as magnets or gamma fuel on any upside break, while also revealing where big money is positioned for the next move.
items.impact: Upside skew and potential gamma support above spot

items.title: Bitcoin Treasury Firms Sell Holdings, Pivot to AI
items.summary: Multiple public bitcoin treasury companies including Strategy imitators, Sequans, Nakamoto and others have sold bitcoin to repay debt, fund operations or buybacks as share prices collapsed. Some miners like MARA and Bitdeer are also selling coins to finance AI data center pivots. This adds potential spot supply overhang and shows the leveraged DAT model under stress after bitcoin’s big drawdown from highs, which traders need to factor into near-term demand-supply balance.
items.impact: Incremental selling pressure and weaker corporate bid narrative

items.title: BitMEX to Permanently Shut Down on September 23
items.summary: The pioneering crypto derivatives exchange that invented perpetual swaps announced it will close operations on September twenty-third after a strategic review, urging users to close positions and withdraw funds. New registrations are already halted and risk limits kick in late August. Market impact should be limited given its tiny current share, but it marks the end of an era and underscores ongoing consolidation among older venues amid competition and regulatory history.
items.impact: Limited direct price effect; industry consolidation signal

items.title: Jobless Claims Plunge to 187K, Far Below Forecasts
items.summary: Initial unemployment claims for the week ending July 18 dropped to 187,000, well under the 212,000 expected and the prior 209,000. This is one of the lowest readings in years and shows the labor market remains extremely tight with no sign of rising layoffs. Traders should care because it reinforces the higher-for-longer rates narrative ahead of next week's FOMC, limiting odds of any near-term Fed easing and supporting the dollar while pressuring risk assets.
items.impact: Supports higher yields and stronger USD, headwind for Bitcoin and equities

items.title: 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits Multi-Month Highs Near 4.70%
items.summary: The US 10-year yield climbed to around 4.70 percent, its highest since early 2025, before easing slightly, amid strong jobs data and surging oil prices from Middle East tensions. Mortgage rates have also risen to their highest levels of 2026. Crypto traders need to watch this because elevated yields raise the opportunity cost of holding non-yielding assets like Bitcoin and tighten financial conditions overall.
items.impact: Higher discount rates and stronger dollar pressure risk assets

items.title: Section 122 Global Tariffs Expire Today
items.summary: The temporary 10 percent import surcharge imposed under Section 122 of the Trade Act of 1974 is set to expire at 12:01 a.m. EDT on July 24 unless extended by Congress, which looks unlikely. This follows earlier court challenges to broader tariff authority. Markets will watch for any replacement measures or trade flow impacts, as lower tariffs could ease some inflation pressure but also signal shifting trade policy under the administration.
items.impact: Potential mild disinflationary effect offset by policy uncertainty

items.title: S&P Global Flash PMIs Due, Focus on Growth and Prices
items.summary: Flash July readings for US manufacturing, services, and composite PMIs are scheduled for release this morning, following solid but uneven June data. Early indications point to continued private-sector expansion, with services potentially stronger while manufacturing cools after prior tariff front-running. These are key for traders as they offer a timely read on economic momentum and inflation pass-through right before the FOMC blackout and next week's rate decision.
items.impact: Data-dependent move in yields and USD depending on beat or miss

items.title: June Building Permits Finalized at 1.374 Million
items.summary: The final reading for June building permits came in at 1.374 million, a bit above the 1.367 million consensus after the preliminary drop. Month-over-month this is still down about 2.6 percent from May. Housing data matters for crypto traders because it feeds into growth and Fed outlook assessments; softer residential activity can eventually cool the economy but current levels remain resilient enough to keep rate-cut hopes in check.
items.impact: Mildly mixed signal for growth, limited immediate market move

items.title: Fed Holds Expected Next Week; Warsh Signals Caution on Inflation
items.summary: Markets fully price a hold at the July 29 FOMC meeting with the funds rate at 3.50-3.75 percent under Chair Kevin Warsh. Recent comments emphasize that prices remain too high, and minutes showed debate over possible hikes amid sticky inflation. With strong claims data and high oil, the bar for cuts is high. This keeps the higher-for-longer backdrop intact for risk assets heading into the decision and press conference.
items.impact: Entrenches elevated rates and USD strength versus Bitcoin

items.title: Trump Vows Major Punishment After Houthi Tanker Attacks
items.summary: Yemen's Houthis struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, extending the US-Iran war to a second key shipping chokepoint and pushing Brent crude above one hundred dollars a barrel. President Trump said any further attacks would bring major military punishment on Iran as their sponsor and on the Houthis themselves, while US forces completed a thirteenth straight night of strikes on Iran. Iran has been retaliating against US bases in the region and tanker traffic through Hormuz hit multi-month lows. Crypto traders should care because energy shocks like this drive inflation fears, raise risk-off pressure, and can hammer risk assets hard in the short term.
items.impact: Oil spike and war escalation drive risk-off selling in crypto and equities

items.title: US Imposes 10-12.5% Tariffs on 60 Trading Partners
items.summary: The Trump administration slapped new ten to twelve point five percent tariffs on goods from sixty major trading partners, covering nearly all US imports, citing failures to ban forced labor products. The duties took effect Friday exactly as temporary ten percent global tariffs expired, hitting the EU, China, Japan and many others with limited exemptions. Trading partners immediately protested the move as unjustified. This keeps trade uncertainty elevated and could slow global growth, which is rarely friendly for risk assets like Bitcoin.
items.impact: Higher trade barriers risk slower growth and persistent market volatility

items.title: Trump Ties Saudi Nuclear Deal to Israel Normalization
items.summary: President Trump declared that the landmark US civilian nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia is fully contingent on Riyadh joining the Abraham Accords and recognizing Israel. The condition was not clearly part of the initial announcement and has created confusion even as White House officials say talks continue. Critics warn it risks nuclear proliferation in the Middle East. For markets this adds another layer of diplomatic uncertainty in an already volatile region that is driving oil prices.
items.impact: Diplomatic complication keeps Middle East risk premium elevated

items.title: Iran Threatens UK RAF Base Used for US Strikes
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards declared RAF Fairford in Britain a legitimate target after the US used the base to launch bombers against Iran. The UK government responded that its forces stand ready around the clock to defend the country. This marks a clear widening of the conflict beyond the Gulf. Traders need to watch for any actual strike that could pull NATO deeper into the war and spike safe-haven flows away from crypto.
items.impact: Risk of wider European involvement heightens geopolitical uncertainty

items.title: House Votes to Curb Trump Iran War Powers
items.summary: The Republican-led House passed legislation directing President Trump to halt military action against Iran without congressional approval, another symbolic rebuke. The Senate blocked a similar measure hours later so the war continues. High oil prices and war costs are putting political pressure on Republicans ahead of midterms. It signals domestic friction over the conflict but does not immediately change the battlefield reality that is moving energy markets.
items.impact: Political constraints on war but no near-term de-escalation expected

items.title: Hormuz Tanker Traffic Hits Lowest in Months
items.summary: Ship-tracking data showed tanker crossings through the Strait of Hormuz dropping to just one vessel on Thursday, the lowest in over two months amid the US-Iran war. Iran continues missile activity near the waterway while the US enforces its own measures. Combined with Red Sea disruptions this is choking two of the world's most critical energy routes. Sustained high oil prices feed into broader inflation and can force risk assets lower until shipping normalizes.
items.impact: Supply disruption sustains elevated oil and inflation fears
